questions.problem: What is the trace in the $yz$-plane of the hyperbolic cylinder $\frac{(x-4)^{2}}{2}-\frac{(y+1)^{2}}{7}=1?$
questions.worked_solution:
To find the trace in the $yz$-plane, we substitute $x=0$ into the equation of the cylinder, and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{(0-4)^{2}}{2}-\frac{(y+1)^{2}}{7} & =1 \\ 8-\frac{(y+1)^{2}}{7} & =1 \\ \frac{(y+1)^{2}}{7} & =7 \\ (y+1)^{2} & =49 \\ y+1 & =\pm 7 \\ y & =-1\pm 7 \\ y & =-8,6\end{aligned}
$$

This gives us the equation of two lines $y=-8$ and $y=6$ in the $yz$-plane.

questions.problem: What is the trace in the $xz$-plane of the elliptic cylinder $\frac{(x-4)^{2}}{8}+\frac{(y-1)^{2}}{2}=1?$
questions.worked_solution:
To find the trace in the $xz$-plane, we substitute $y=0$ into the equation of the cylinder, and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{(x-4)^{2}}{8}+\frac{(0-1)^{2}}{2} & =1 \\ \frac{(x-4)^{2}}{8}+\frac{1}{2} & =1 \\ \frac{(x-4)^{2}}{8} & =\frac{1}{2} \\ (x-4)^{2} & =4 \\ x-4 & =\pm 2 \\ x & =4\pm 2 \\ x & =2,6\end{aligned}
$$

This gives us the equation of two lines $x=2$ and $x=6$ in the $xz$-plane.

questions.problem: What is the domain in the $xy$-plane of the hyperbolic cylinder $\frac{{x}^{2}}{3}-\frac{(y+1)^{2}}{4}=1?$
questions.worked_solution:
The full expression describing all points on our hyperbolic cylinder is

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}}{3}-\frac{(y+1)^{2}}{4}=1,\,z=k
$$

where $k\in R$ can vary arbitrarily. 

The domain of any cylinder in the $xy$-plane is its base curve. Hence, in this case, the domain is

$$
\{(x,y)\in {R}^{2}:\text{ }\frac{{x}^{2}}{3}-\frac{(y+1)^{2}}{4}=1\}.
$$

This is a hyperbola centered at $(0,-1).$

questions.problem: What is the domain in the $xy$-plane of the parabolic cylinder $(x-1)^{2}=3y?$
questions.worked_solution:
The full expression describing all points on our parabolic cylinder is

$$
(x-1)^{2}=3y,\,z=k
$$

where $k\in R$ can vary arbitrarily. 

The domain of any cylinder in the $xy$-plane is its base curve. Hence, in this case, the domain is

$$
\{(x,y)\in {R}^{2}:(x-1)^{2}=3y\}.
$$

This is an upward-opening parabola with a vertex at $(1,0).$

$$
{x}^{2}=-5(y+1),\,z=k

The domain of any cylinder in the $xy$-plane is its base curve. Hence, in this case, the domain is

$$
\{(x,y)\in {R}^{2}:{x}^{2}=-5(y+1)\}.
$$

This is a downward-opening parabola with a vertex at $(0,-1).$
